sourceObservations.observations: Actual pixels show plant tau=M(q)qdd+V+G+F, matched alpha=M(q), beta=V+G+F.
Servo uses E=q_d-q and positive K_v Edot,K_p E before M(q); nominal error has zero right side.

Sensors and commands update at discrete instants; sampling adds delay/approximation and faster sampling makes continuous-time assumption more reasonable. No rule equates repeating a stored value with a new measurement.
Feedforward block uses desired trajectory, feedback adds torque gains outside dynamic model; tau=tau_ff+K_p E+K_v Edot.
Printed homogeneous equation has left products M^-1 K_v and M^-1 K_p. Inertia depends on actual configuration; no full forcing residual printed here.

Disturbance arrow subtracts tau_d at arm input. E=q_d-q reverses actual-acceleration perturbation, giving positive M^-1 tau_d in error. The steady-state formula evaluates M at equilibrium; transient uses current q.

independentAnswers.reasoning: Shorter update intervals may reduce sampling approximation but do not identify mass parameters or remove discrete stability/delay checks. Reusing a stored reading supplies no new physical measurement, regardless of faster controller cycles. The prior oversampling counterexample no longer applies to this changed alternative.

For diagonal D, (M^-1 D)_ij=(M^-1)_ij D_jj. Nonzero off-diagonals of the inverse generally remain, and factors do not generally commute. The stated homogeneous approximation supplies the exact scope; no nonzero forcing residual is needed for this key.

The disturbance reduces actual acceleration by M(q(t))^-1 tau_d. Because Edd=qdd_d-qdd, its contribution to Edd is positive. Only a steady-equilibrium specialization freezes M at q_e; the transient equation uses the current configuration.

assertions: left gain product retains off diagonals
